subject: Data Structure and Algorithm
chapters: Chapter 2: Linear Data Structures: Stacks and Queues

questions.text: Define Data Structure. Differentiate between Primitive vs Non-Primitive, and Linear vs Non-Linear data structures with examples.
Explain Abstract Data Type (ADT). Explain Time and Space Complexity analysis using Big-O, Big-Omega, and Big-Theta asymptotic notations.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Linear Data Structures: Stacks and Queues
questions.text: Define Stack ADT. Explain Stack operations (PUSH, POP, PEEK) with algorithm and array implementation. Explain Overflow and Underflow conditions.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Linear Data Structures: Stacks and Queues
questions.text: Convert the Infix expression: `(A + B) * C - (D - E) ^ (F + G)` into Postfix and Prefix expressions using Stack algorithm.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Linear Data Structures: Stacks and Queues
questions.text: Define Circular Queue. Explain why a Linear Queue suffers from false overflow. Write C functions to enqueue and dequeue elements in a Circular Queue.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Linear Data Structures: Stacks and Queues
questions.text: Explain Priority Queue and Deque (Input Restricted and Output Restricted Deque) with their practical applications.
Define Linked List. Compare Static Memory Allocation (Arrays) vs Dynamic Memory Allocation (Linked Lists) in terms of insertion, deletion, and access time.
Write C functions for Singly Linked List: (a) Insert node at beginning, (b) Insert node at specified position, and (c) Delete node from end.
Explain Doubly Linked List and Circular Linked List with node structure definitions and memory pointer diagrams.
Implement Stack and Queue data structures using Singly Linked List.
Define Binary Tree, Full Binary Tree, and Complete Binary Tree. Explain Tree Traversals: Inorder, Preorder, and Postorder recursively with C code snippets.
Define Binary Search Tree (BST). Construct a BST by inserting keys: 45, 15, 79, 90, 10, 55, 12, 20, 50. Write algorithm to search and delete a key from BST.
Explain AVL Tree and Balance Factor. Explain AVL rotations: LL, RR, LR, and RL rotations with numerical step-by-step insertion examples.
Explain B-Tree and B+ Tree properties, structure, and applications in database indexing.
Define Graph. Differentiate between Adjacency Matrix and Adjacency List representations in terms of space complexity and edge lookup time.
Explain Graph Traversal algorithms: Breadth-First Search (BFS) using Queue and Depth-First Search (DFS) using Stack with algorithms and step-by-step trace.
Define Minimum Spanning Tree (MST). Explain Prim's Algorithm and Kruskal's Algorithm for finding MST with step-by-step numerical trace on a sample weighted graph.
Explain Dijkstra's Algorithm for Single Source Shortest Path problem with algorithm and trace on a sample directed weighted graph.
Differentiate between Linear Search and Binary Search algorithms. Derive the Best, Average, and Worst case time complexity of Binary Search.
Explain Quick Sort algorithm using Divide and Conquer strategy. Trace Quick Sort on array: [38, 27, 43, 3, 9, 82, 10] using the last element as pivot.
Explain Merge Sort algorithm. Derive its recurrence relation $T(n) = 2T(n/2) + O(n)$ and solve using master theorem.
Explain Heap Sort algorithm. Define Max-Heap and Min-Heap. Build a Max-Heap for keys: [12, 11, 13, 5, 6, 7] and perform heapify and deletion operations.
Define Hashing, Hash Table, and Hash Function. Explain properties of a good hash function (Division method, Multiplication method, Mid-Square method).
Explain Hash Collisions. Compare Collision Resolution Techniques: Open Addressing (Linear Probing, Quadratic Probing, Double Hashing) vs Chaining (Separate Chaining).
